chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Salt, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"It is not appropriate to stand (waqf) under the arak trees; as for staying/resting under them until the sun sets and one rises to proceed to the standing place (Arafat), there is no objection."

key_terms.الْأَرَكَ: Arak trees (Shorea robusta, common in Arafat)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on standing or resting under the arak trees during Hajj at Arafat?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical etiquette of the Standing at Arafat (Waqf Arafat) by distinguishing between the ritual act of standing and casual resting under the shade of arak trees. It permits staying under the trees until the sun declines to prepare for the departure, reflecting the scholarly consensus that the essential condition is the duration of presence rather than the specific posture or location, thereby facilitating the comfort of pilgrims during the intense heat of the plains.
